name: Orisha, Ayelala
body:
AYELALA
CR 18

A timelessly radiant woman clad in white robes, adorned with cowries and beads. She carries a water pot and wields a knife.

XP 153,600
Unique LG Medium outsider (good, lawful, orisha)
Init +11; Senses darkvision 60 ft., know the truth, see invisibility, true seeing; Perception +32

DEFENSE

AC 33, touch 27, flat-footed 25 (+4 armor, +7 Dex, +1 dodge, +9 insight, +2 natural)
hp 290 (20d10+180); regeneration 10 (evil)
Fort +16, Ref +19, Will +21
Defensive Abilities graceful movement, divine grace; DR 15/evil; Immune mind-affecting effects; Resist acid 30, cold 30, electricity 30, fire 30; SR 29

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee oath razor +29/+24/+19/+14 (1d4+9/15–20 plus retributive knife)
Special Attacks mark transgressor, retributive knife
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 20th; concentration +29; save DCs are Wis-based)

Constant—see invisibility, true seeing
At will—air walk, augury, bestow curse (DC 22), commune, confusion (DC 23), divination, dream, geas/quest (DC 25), zone of truth (DC 21)
3/day—quickened reach greater bestow curseap82 (DC 25), insanity (DC 26), insect plague, summon natures ally VI

STATISTICS

Str 18, Dex 25, Con 26, Int 18, Wis 29, Cha 21
Base Atk +20; CMB +24; CMD 51
Feats Combat Casting, Combat Reflexes, Dodge, Great Fortitude, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Quicken Spell-Like Ability (greater bestow curse), Reach Spell-like Ability (greater bestow curse), Spring Attack, Toughness
Skills Diplomacy +28, Intimidate +28, Knowledge (arcana) +27, Knowledge (history) +27, Knowledge (local) +27, Knowledge (planes) +27, Knowledge (religion) +27, Perception +32, Sense Motive +32, Spellcraft +27
Languages Celestial, Common; truespeech

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Divine Grace (Su)

Ayelala adds her Charisma modifier as an insight bonus to AC.

Graceful Movement (Su)

When Ayelala moves at half speed, she ignores difficult terrain and her movement does not provoke attacks of opportunity.

Know the Truth (Su)

Ayelala knows when she hears a lie. This functions as discern lies, but with no saving throw, and affects all creatures that ayelala can hear. This automatically bypasses all magical effects that conceal falsehoods, such as glibness, except those used by the gods themselves.

Mark Transgressor (Su)

As a move or swift action, Ayelala can mark a creature see can see and knows is a criminal. Ayelala gains a +5 bonus on Knowledge, Perception, and Sense Motive checks attempted against that creature, and a +5 bonus on weapon attack and damage rolls against it. The DCs of her spell-like abilities against that opponent increases by 5. Ayelala have up to five creatures designated in this way at a time. If she exceeds that number, she chooses one creature to no longer be marked. Ayelala can also unmark a creature as a free action.

Oath Razor (Su)

Ayelala’s knife functions as a +5 keen kukri but only for her.

Retributive Knife (Su)

Any creature hit by ayelala’s knife suffers visions of any wrongdoings they’ve committed. They take an additional 10d6 damage and are confused for 1 round. A successful DC 25 Will save halves damage and negates the confusion. A creature confused by this ability doesn’t attack ayelala even if compelled to attack the closest creature. This is a mind-affecting effect. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any
Organization solitary
Treasure standard (+3 silken ceremonial armor, dagger, other treasure)

Ayelala is the Orisha of divination, justice, oaths, and truth.

She delivers justice and swift retribution against those who commit criminal offenses. She strikes fear in those who knowingly steal, commit sexual offences, or other crimes that cry out for justice.

Ayelala punishes oath-breakers and wrongdoers with sickness, madness, or even death. She may dispatch bees, scorpions, snakes, or other venomous creatures to sting the transgressor. Madness is another form of her punishment, exhibited by erratic behavior, hallucinations, or public shame.

Her manifestations often compel wrongdoers to confess.

She immediately knows the truthfulness of anyone’s words and may extend leniency to those who unwittingly commit offenses. Ayelala is known to deeply reflect on the root of an ongoing problem, deriving the cause and possible solution after consideration. In dreams, she often takes the form of an elderly woman garlanded in sacred ornaments, or as a natural creature she uses to punish, such as a bee, scorpion, or snake.
